key_insight: AutoDex automates the full real-world data collection loop for dexterous grasping, making it possible to generate and verify large-scale grasp data on hardware instead of relying on slow teleoperation or unverifiable simulation. The result is a more scalable way to collect physically valid grasp outcomes for training robust manipulation systems.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the bottleneck of acquiring large-scale, real-world dexterous grasping data with verified physical outcomes. Existing methods are either too slow and biased (teleoperation) or scalable but not physically trustworthy (simulation).
method: Generates candidate dexterous grasps automatically from perception and grasp proposal components.
Executes grasp attempts on real hardware to verify physical contact success or failure.
Automates the end-to-end pipeline for perception, execution, labeling, and resampling to reduce human intervention.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in robotics, AutoDex provides a practical path to building larger, cleaner training datasets for dexterous manipulation. This can improve policy learning, reduce sim-to-real gaps, and accelerate research on robust real-world grasping.

paper_title: AutoDex: An Automated Real-World System for Dexterous Grasping Data Collection
paper_authors: Mingi Choi, Gunhee Kim, Jisoo Kim, Taeksoo Kim, Taeyun Ha
